en.summary: The United Kingdom has a highly competitive national press concentrated in London and a public broadcaster, the BBC, that is one of the world's most-used news sources. National newspapers range from subscription titles such as The Times, the Financial Times and The Telegraph to The Guardian, which is owned by a trust and free to read online. Broadcast news also includes ITV, Channel 4 and Sky News, all subject to impartiality rules set by the regulator Ofcom. Investigative reporting comes from newspapers, broadcasters and nonprofit bureaus, and an independent charity leads national fact-checking. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have their own newspapers and political coverage. Newspapers mostly self-regulate through the Independent Press Standards Organisation. Many regional newspapers have consolidated under a few large publishers.

faq.q: What are the main national news outlets in the United Kingdom?
faq.a: The main national outlets in the directory include BBC News, The Guardian, The Times, Financial Times and The Telegraph. The Top National News column lists them in editorial order.

faq.q: Which British news sites are free to read?
faq.a: Free-to-read outlets include BBC News, The Guardian, The Independent, Sky News and ITV News. The paywall model of every outlet is shown next to its name.

faq.q: Which British outlets are publicly or state funded?
faq.a: Public-service outlets include BBC News, Channel 4 News and BBC Sport. Ownership is labeled on every outlet in the directory.

faq.q: Where can I find regional news in the United Kingdom?
faq.a: Regional coverage in the directory comes from Manchester Evening News (Greater Manchester), The Scotsman (Scotland), The Herald (Scotland), Belfast Telegraph (Northern Ireland) and WalesOnline (Wales). The Regional & Local column lists every regional outlet.

general-news.intro: These are the outlets most used to follow national news in the United Kingdom, from the BBC and international wire services to national newspapers with different paywall models.

economy.intro: British business journalism is anchored in the City of London, with a global business daily, a weekly economics magazine and outlets covering markets and personal finance.

sports.intro: UK sports media covers the Premier League, cricket, rugby, tennis and Formula 1, through public and private broadcasters, a sports radio station and subscription beat reporting.

investigative.intro: Investigative journalism in the UK comes from a satirical magazine with a long record of scoops, nonprofit bureaus, an independent fact-checking charity and broadcast teams.

politics.intro: Westminster politics is covered by national newspapers, weekly political magazines, a talk radio station and specialized parliamentary news sites.

regional.intro: Regional outlets cover Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland and English cities such as Manchester, each with its own political institutions and news agenda.
